candidate_digest_recipe: git ls-files plus git ls-files --others --exclude-standard, sorted; sha256 over, for each path in order, the UTF-8 path bytes followed by the RAW 32-byte sha256 digest (not its hex text) of the file content. This manifest IS included. Its contribution is the sha256 of json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) with ONLY THE FIELD BEING COMPUTED blanked to the empty string - that one field at the top level and in every acceptance_rounds entry. The other digest keeps its real value. Computing tested_candidate_digest blanks tested_candidate_digest alone; evidence_bundle_digest is still empty at that point, so nothing is lost. Computing evidence_bundle_digest blanks evidence_bundle_digest alone; tested_candidate_digest is already frozen, so the evidence digest depends on it. That dependency IS the binding between the evidence and the input the acceptance streams judged. An earlier form blanked BOTH fields, on the stated rationale that naming a single field would be self-referentially impossible once the second field held a value. That rationale was wrong: each field is computed at a moment when the other is either empty or already frozen, so both directions are deterministic. The consequence was measured, not argued - under blank-both, three different tested_candidate_digest values produced one identical evidence digest, so the field naming which tree was judged could hold any 64-hex string forever while every check stayed silent. Found by independent review, at exactly the place the surrounding prose claimed a binding the arithmetic could not provide.

digest_model.tested_candidate_digest: Frozen BEFORE the acceptance streams start. It identifies the immutable input they judge. Recorded here once the streams are dispatched and never edited afterwards; if it must change, the round is void and a new one begins.
digest_model.evidence_bundle_digest: Computed AFTER the results are written. It identifies the tree that carries the acceptance evidence. It necessarily differs from tested_candidate_digest, because writing PASS into the tree changes the tree.
digest_model.why_split: An earlier form recorded one digest, computed after the acceptance records were written. It therefore identified the post-acceptance evidence tree rather than the input the streams actually judged - the acceptance appeared to certify a tree that did not exist when it ran. Found by independent review.
digest_model.artifact_manifest_sha256: Unrelated to both. It certifies the four reviewed families unchanged and is deliberately invariant across rebuilds that leave the contracts alone.
digest_model.round_scoped: Both digests are recorded twice: at the top level for the current round, and inside the matching acceptance_rounds entry as history. Without the per-round copy a retro-edit of the top-level value and a genuine new round would be indistinguishable, so 'frozen and never edited afterwards' would not be checkable. Named by the QA author, who declined to write a test asserting a property the structure could not support.

recorded_limits.evidence_report_visibility: The acceptance digests enumerate git ls-files --exclude-standard, so a report path added to .gitignore leaves the digest and every check silent about its content - an independent reviewer demonstrated a fabricated manual report passing that way. It is a declared scope limit rather than a hidden hole: the attack requires editing .gitignore, which is tracked and inside the digest, so it appears in the diff a reviewer reads. The next task touching the QA module must assert that both report paths are tracked and not ignored; it is not opened as its own round because the current mechanism makes the manoeuvre visible rather than invisible.
recorded_limits.prefix_widening_unpinned: ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_PREFIX and RATIFIABLE_REVIEWED_PREFIX are unpinned in the widening direction only; the guarantee is that report paths are confined to some declared prefix, not that the prefix is the narrow one. That property is what was established and it stands. The failure counts this entry used to carry - 'narrowing is caught, at 38 and 9 failures respectively' - are withdrawn, not replaced, for three reasons found in sequence. First, they were written from a measurement of an earlier tree and never re-measured. Second, an independent re-measurement disagreed with both. Third, and worst: the attribution was wrong as well as the number. W0-QA-01.md section 8 describes the 38 as ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_PREFIX 'moved out of artifacts/ altogether', and records that widening it to artifacts/ or artifacts/checkpoints/ leaves the suite green. This entry called that same figure a narrowing, which is a different edit. So the record carried two independent drifts on one number, and replacing the count would have left the false attribution in place. Any restatement must name the tree it was taken on and the exact mutation that produced it: section 8's own figures are against a 281-test suite and the frozen candidate runs 324, so every count differs for that reason alone, before any drift. Owner: W1. See W0-QA-01.md section 8 item 18 and section 11.18.5.
recorded_limits.dynamic_dispatch_unenumerable: eval, importlib and getattr with a computed name cannot be resolved by the module's static spawn enumeration. Recorded rather than chased: a test module does not outrank its own author. See W0-QA-01.md section 8 item 17.
recorded_limits.digest_covers_untracked_files: candidate_digest_recipe enumerates git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, so the value stops reproducing from the working tree the moment either acceptance stream writes its report. recorded_limits.unfrozen_round_state: Between a void and the next freeze the checkpoint has no frozen tested_candidate_digest and the top-level field is null, which is the honest value: the current round has identified no input yet. Several probes in tests/contract/test_cp00_candidate.py build their sandboxes out of the live repository's frozen digest and cannot construct themselves without one, so the unfrozen state is one that module is only now learning to model; that coupling belongs to the same QA remediation that aligns the post-freeze ceiling. Measured on 2026-09-04 against the working copy of that module: with this manifest, _tested_digest_problems, _acceptance_problems, _post_freeze_delta_problems, _state_document_problems, _publication_record_problems, _task_banner_problems and _checkpoint_bundle_problems are all empty and _freeze_commit is correctly None. The alternative was measured rather than argued: carrying the voided round's digest forward at the top level makes _tested_digest_problems report a digest frozen at no commit and _acceptance_problems report the top level disagreeing with the current round's entry, besides naming the previous round's tree as the input the next streams will judge.
recorded_limits.state_record_sweep: artifacts/checkpoints/CP-00/check_state_records.py is the completeness check for two axes: a superseded QA evidence commit presented as current, and stale round accounting - which acceptance round is owed, and how many are in the record. Both are bound to the structural unit containing an occurrence - the enclosing JSON object or string value under its key trail, the enclosing table row, or the enclosing sentence - not to a line window, because a window is proximity rather than attribution and the earlier form exited 0 on the very tree it was written for. The round-accounting axis derives its truth from current_round and acceptance_rounds in this manifest instead of restating them, so the sweep cannot itself go stale; four records must state both claims in a form the check can read, so a document that says nothing does not pass for the wrong reason; and nothing is skipped by path except the dated primary acceptance reports and the checker itself. Both axes are measured rather than asserted: --rev sweeps any commit's objects without a checkout, and the axis-one findings at bde3af3, a3eaf88 and 5b70ee4 are 1, 1 and 4. --selftest proves each axis-two detector fires and that a history label excuses only the unit containing it. Limits: it checks the owed round and the round count, not each round's recorded verdict; and a claim inside a per-round entry or an object carrying superseded_by is treated as dated history and not swept.
